gen-dafont-college-gf-hind-madurai: College hits with a dynamic, authoritative punch, every curve as heavy as its stems. Hind Madurai follows in a plain sans whose wide-mouthed s and capital-sized lowercase make long paragraphs feel approachable and unhurried.
gen-dafont-college-gf-hind-mysuru: Tall, dense and confident, College leans on big counters and uniform strokes. And Hind Mysuru, a contemporary sans with lowercase pressing toward the ascender line, gives that weight a steadier, more conversational partner underneath.
gen-dafont-college-gf-hind-siliguri: Authoritative, that's College, with fat counters and strokes that never thin out. Hind Siliguri brings a sans-serif texture of constant line weight and gently gapped rounds, so extended reading settles into a smooth, approachable gray.
gen-dafont-college-gf-hind-vadodara: College draws every curve as heavy as a straight stem, leaving big counters inside a tall lowercase. It stuns at display scale, while Hind Vadodara's sans-serif letters stay spacious and open for the quieter text.
gen-dafont-college-gf-huninn: Huninn reads modern and tidy, its lowercase rising close to cap height. Give it a comfortable body size and let College, with its heavy, uniform curves and big counters, handle the loud work.
gen-dafont-college-gf-inter-tight: Inter Tight reads modern and compact, a plain sans with short ascenders and curve tails held back. And College adds the dynamic, authoritative weight up top, its uniform curves and big counters giving the text something to answer to.
gen-dafont-college-gf-karla: Karla reads modern and friendly, with a gaping c and a middle band so tall the lines look stocky. Against College's one-nib heft, a longer stretch of text feels relaxed.
gen-dafont-college-gf-kedebideri: Kedebideri brings a skyward x-height and rounded, inviting letters, all neutral and approachable. But College earns its keep big and short, where stems and crossbars sharing one thickness give it a dynamic, authoritative punch.
gen-dafont-college-gf-khula: College is a dynamic display face drawn like a skeleton outline given one fixed stroke thickness. Khula, a plain sans with a tall midsection and open-mouthed curves, does the quiet work of carrying text while College makes the statement.
gen-dafont-college-gf-krub: Krub reads contemporary and neutral, with a pronounced x-height and curves that lift off before closing the loop. College, meanwhile, keeps every stroke free of heavy-to-light shifts, so its authority sits above that lighter text without crowding it.
